results.description: Land with at least 15% battery remaining

findings.summary: Estimated battery remaining fell to 0% at 11:15:19Z (T+579.2s). Below 15% most operations manuals require immediate landing; below 7% the vehicle is at imminent risk of power loss and uncontrolled descent.
findings.title: Battery depleted to 0% in flight

evidence.note: baseline: highest voltage in the preceding 10 s
voltage at worst sag (51% below baseline)

findings.summary: Battery voltage fell from 26.0 V to 12.8 V within 10.0 s, reaching the low point at 11:15:27Z (T+587.8s) (51% below the recent baseline). Current was 39.7 A at the baseline sample and 31.6 A at the sag point. Normal discharge cannot explain a drop this fast; it indicates the pack could not hold voltage under load (high internal resistance, a failing or cold cell, overload, or a power-system fault), which can cut power before the remaining-capacity estimate reaches zero.

threshold.basis: heuristic: drop below the highest voltage in the preceding 10 s. Healthy LiPo packs typically sag well under 10% on a load step; 15%+ suggests high internal resistance, a failing cell, a cold pack or overload

findings.title: Voltage sag under load (51% within 10 s)

evidence.note: final logged height (above home) while armed

findings.summary: The log terminates while the vehicle is still armed at approximately 14.2 m above home. Flight logs normally continue until disarm; an in-air truncation is consistent with sudden power loss, controller brownout, or destruction of the vehicle at impact. The final logged data point is at 11:15:34Z (T+594.6s).
findings.title: Log ends in flight (possible power loss / brownout / impact)

findings.summary: Two independent altitude sensors disagree. After correcting for their initial reference offset (+20.4 m), barometric altitude and GPS altitude diverged by up to 20.3 m at 11:15:20Z (T+580.5s). At least one of them is wrong at that moment. Typical causes: barometer error from airflow or temperature, GPS multipath or poor satellite geometry, or estimator divergence. Altitude-dependent conclusions near this time must state which source they rely on. 1 of 1190 comparison points were skipped because one source had no sample within 1.0 s (treated as a data gap, not compared).
findings.title: barometric altitude and GPS altitude diverged by 20.3 m

findings.summary: The flight controller's state estimator (EKF) reported a magnetometer/heading innovation test ratio peaking at 2.38 at 11:15:18Z (T+578.4s) (0.3% of in-flight samples above 1.0, 1.1% above 0.5). A ratio above 1.0 means the estimator was actively rejecting that sensor's measurements because they disagreed with its state estimate — the vehicle's believed magnetometer/heading and the measured magnetometer/heading were in conflict.
findings.title: Estimator rejected magnetometer/heading measurements (peak ratio 2.38)
